top.line: Our iOS builds waited three times longer than they ran, on a pool of five Macs.
top.para: One Mac job per push, then one integrated build an hour, brought push to TestFlight under half an hour.

in-short.line: Macs not agents, ten Macs per push, measured and rebuilt, flooded again, where it stands.

series.line: Part five of the Ten days series, after native apps by agents.

diagnosis.line: On 10 November I saw that allocating Macs was the bottleneck and asked for fewer steps and publishing from dev.
diagnosis.para: An agent was asked to measure it.

measured.line: 579 runs: 6,980 Mac-minutes run, 22,427 queued; the five-Mac pool full most of the time.
measured.para: A median of ten macOS jobs per dev push; 47.5 minutes to TestFlight.

reasons.line: Separate Macs per step, cold starts, sequential stages, untested uploads, idle Macs, side branches.
reasons.para: 821 jobs cancelled before they got a Mac.

one-mac.line: All Mac work in one job: build, test on iPhone and iPad, publish only when green.
one-mac.para: Build before booting simulators; a generic simulator destination; one shared build folder.

flood.line: On 15 November the runners flooded again; the fix was a rule: one integrated build an hour.
flood.para: Night builds from about 35 minutes to about 7.

now.line: A live CI status page; push to processed in TestFlight in about 20 to 25 minutes.
now.para: Seven news app builds overnight; larger runners still to decide.

lessons.line: Shared machines do not scale with agents; measure first; fewer jobs; rules; show the number.

limits.line: The agent's measurements, two after runs, the conductor's approximate night notes, no pricing.

sources.line: The iOS repository's briefs, commits and workflows, and the live CI status page.
